Download • Features • Keybinds • Screenshots • Data • Files • Development • Contributing • License

> tickr is a stock watcher and trading practice app for the Windows tray and > macOS menu bar. Hover over the tray icon for a quote, or use a global hotkey > to open charts, watchlists, alerts and market research. Compare two charts, > replay historical candles, and practice trades with simulated orders or > randomly selected setups.

## Download Get the latest installer from [Releases](https://github.com/joezhuo2/tickr/releases/latest): - **Windows:** `tickr_x.y.z_x64-setup.exe`. Installs per user, no admin prompt. - **macOS:** `tickr_x.y.z_universal.dmg` (Apple silicon and Intel), macOS 10.15 or later. Drag tickr into Applications. ### First launch tickr is not code-signed yet, so both systems warn the first time you open it. The builds come from the public [release workflow](.github/workflows/release.yml), so you can check what went into them. - **Windows:** SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC". Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. You only see this once. - **macOS 15 (Sequoia) or later:** open tickr and close the warning that it can't be verified. Go to **System Settings > Privacy & Security**, scroll down to the message about tickr and click **Open Anyway**, then confirm with your password. - **macOS 14 or earlier:** right-click tickr in Applications, choose **Open**, then **Open** again. - **macOS says tickr "is damaged and can't be opened":** the download was quarantined. Run this, then open it again: ```bash xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/tickr.app ``` ### Updates From v0.5.1, tickr updates itself. It checks GitHub 30 seconds after launch and every 12 hours. When a new version is out, the tray tooltip says so and the update item in the tray menu reads **Install vX.Y.Z and restart**. Nothing installs until you click it. tickr then downloads the update, checks its signature against the key built into the app, installs it and restarts. The first-launch warnings above don't come back after an update. **Check for updates** checks right away. Turn off **Check for updates automatically** to stop the background checks. Versions before v0.5.1 can't update themselves: install v0.5.1 once from Releases. ## Features - **Display settings:** choose System, Light or Dark, text size from 100% to 150%, and standard or accessible blue/orange gain and loss colors. Changes apply immediately and are saved. ### Tray and hotkey - **Tray icon:** the company logo with an up/down badge. Hover for the quote, left-click to open the window, or to close it again the way the hotkey does if it's already open and focused. Right-click holds every on/off setting: show pre-market/after-hours, show change as % or $, always on top, unload window when minimized, start hidden, launch at login, check for updates automatically and, on macOS, show price in menu bar. If something needs attention (the hotkey is taken, or launch at login could not be changed), the tooltip ends with a ⚠ line. - **Global hotkey** (default `Ctrl+Alt+K` on Windows, `⌘⇧K` on macOS): opens the window, or minimizes it if it's focused. On macOS, where tickr has no Dock icon, it hides the window instead (or unloads it, when unload is on). Change it in [Settings](#settings-and-keybinds). If another app owns the hotkey at startup, the window footer shows the error until you pick one that works. - **Launch at login** is off until you turn it on. Once on, it survives upgrades: tickr re-registers itself if an installer removed the entry, unless you turned it off in Task Manager. - **Unload when minimized** (on by default): minimizing destroys the web view, so the app drops to one process using about 7 MB. The hotkey reopens it already painted with the last chart and quote, then refreshes in the background. The window opens on a dark or light background to match the OS theme, so it never flashes white. Windows may hide new tray icons in the overflow menu (^). Drag it onto the taskbar to keep it visible. ### Chart - **Symbol and range:** search to change the symbol, pick a range from 1D to Max and switch between line and candles. Search filters by asset type and exchange, and exact ticker matches come first. Press Enter on a typed ticker to open it directly. 1D, 5D and 1M charts reload about once a minute. - **Sessions and time zone:** extended-hours candles can be shown or hidden on the chart without changing the tray quote setting. Pre- and post-market sessions are shaded, and chart times can use the exchange or local time zone. - **Second chart:** the toggle (J by default) opens a second chart pane, side by side or stacked, with its own symbol and range. Crosshair time is linked across both charts. Turn on **Sync** to pan and zoom both panes together. tickr saves the layout across launches. - **Recent symbols and history:** focus the empty search box to see the last 10 symbols you viewed. The Back and Forward buttons (or Alt+Left and Alt+Right) step through this session's symbols, and B jumps to the previous one, so pressing it again toggles between two. - **Price scales:** linear, logarithmic, or percentage change rebased to the first visible candle as you pan and zoom. Press L to cycle scales. - **Drawings:** the toolbar places levels, trendlines, text and freehand pen strokes, saved per symbol. Keys 1 to 5 pick the level, trendline, text, ruler and pen tools. Drag to move them or adjust trend endpoints, and Delete removes the selection. Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes, and Escape returns to Cursor. The ruler measures price, percent, bars and elapsed time without saving. - **Candle interval:** choose Auto to keep the default resolution for each range, or select a supported interval independently. The choice is saved and resets to Auto when switching to a range that does not support it. - **Tooltip:** hover the chart, or use ← and →, for time, open, high, low, close and volume. - **Zoom and pan:** scroll or pinch to zoom at the cursor (down to 10 bars), drag or scroll sideways to pan, and double-click to see the whole range again. With the chart focused, + and - zoom and 0 resets. The price axis fits the visible bars, and a zoomed view follows new bars at the right edge. - **Event dots** along the bottom of the chart; hover the candle for details: | Dot | Marks | | --- | --- | | Blue | Earnings report: quarter and EPS vs estimate (last four quarters) | | Orange | Analyst initiation, upgrade or downgrade: firm, ratings, new target | | Yellow | One of the 20 latest headlines | | Green | Ex-dividend date and amount (6M to Max) | | Purple | Stock split and ratio (6M to Max) | Dots stack when a candle has more than one. A news dot gets a smaller inner circle: green when that candle's headlines lean positive, red when they lean negative, and plain when neutral. Earnings, news and rating dots can be turned off in Settings. - **Exports:** hover the chart for two buttons at its top left. One copies the chart as a PNG image, the other its candles as CSV (time in UTC, open, high, low, close, volume). A button turns green once the copy lands. - **Refresh:** the button in the bottom bar fetches the quote and reloads the chart right away, then force-reloads the panel on screen (News, Earnings, Stats, Financials, Analysts, Events, Market, Options or the Watchlist cards). The bar says " refreshed" or shows the error, and a failed refresh keeps what was already shown. **Background refresh** in Settings defaults to **Balanced**: quotes update every 15 seconds during regular trading, 60 seconds pre/post-market, and 15 minutes when closed. **Low-power** keeps that cadence while visible and slows it to 60 seconds, 5 minutes, and 30 minutes while hidden or minimized. Armed alerts keep their usual 15-second cadence in either mode. Low-power pauses automatic minute chart and watchlist refreshes while hidden and refreshes stale data when shown. Quotes also refresh promptly after system wake or network recovery. ### Replay and trading practice - **Bar replay** (`Y`) starts at a historical date you choose. Play at an adjustable speed or step forward and back one candle at a time. Indicators use only the candles you've revealed. tickr hides live quotes and research panels during the session. - **Paper trading** (`H`) simulates market, limit and stop orders for long and short positions. Set commission and slippage, track realized and unrealized P&L, and review fills on the chart. The account used with current quotes is saved to `paper.json`. Replay uses a separate account for the session, and simulated market orders fill at the next revealed candle's open. - **Random historical practice** (`Q`) draws a symbol and starting point from your watchlist or a group, using the candle interval and date range you pick. Choose **Long**, **Short** or **Skip** with future candles hidden. Close at a revealed candle's close to see your return, bars held and how you did against skipping the trade. ### Views Each tab or button below swaps the chart out; click it again, or a range, to go back. Views fade in, the watchlist slides up, Settings scales open and switching line / candles fades the chart. With the OS reduced-motion setting on, all of it is instant. - **Technicals:** click **Analyze** to run RSI, moving averages, candlestick patterns and volatility/Fibonacci targets on the candles of the selected range, on your machine (same candles, same result). You get a score from −100 to +100 with a bias and confidence, upside and downside targets for the next 10 bars, an invalidation level and the signals behind the score. Checkboxes toggle moving averages, Bollinger bands, VWAP, Fibonacci levels, targets, pattern markers, RSI and MACD panes. Indicator settings let you edit lengths, colors (or reset to the theme), and individual line visibility, with up to eight SMA and eight EMA lines. MACD defaults to 12/26/9 and starts hidden. Settings and up to 50 named presets persist across launches; saving an existing name replaces that preset. Display settings never change the score, signals, or targets, which retain their fixed indicator lengths. Analysis refreshes when new candles arrive. Enable **Keep analysis on** to also run it at startup and after symbol, range or interval changes; otherwise those changes clear the results until you click Analyze again. Overlay visibility is preserved. VWAP resets each day on intraday charts and is anchored to the first candle on daily and longer intervals. Short histories show warm-up estimates and reduced confidence. Computed locally; not investment advice. - **Analysts:** the rating (Strong buy to Sell), average 12-month target and its upside also sit under the price on the left. The tab adds the target range against the current price and the count of each rating. Cached for 12 hours; ETFs, indices and crypto have no coverage. - **Earnings:** the next report date (confirmed or estimated) with EPS and revenue estimates, and the last four quarters with estimate, actual and surprise % (green beat, red miss). - **Stats:** key statistics in Valuation, Trading, Dividends & splits, Shares & short interest, Profitability and Financials. ETFs get a Fund section and crypto a Crypto section. Changes, growth and returns are green or red. - **Financials:** revenue, net income, free cash flow and gross, operating and net margins over the reported periods, with an Annual / Quarterly toggle, two small trend charts and a table. Margins are computed from revenue, and figures Yahoo does not report show as —. Cached for 12 hours; ETFs, indices and crypto have no statements. - **News feed:** choose Watchlist or a named group in News to combine headlines, deduplicate stories and filter by ticker, publisher and topic. - **News:** the 20 latest headlines, newest first, with publisher, time and a Positive / Negative / Neutral pill. The sentiment is guessed on your machine from the headline's words, so take it as a hint. Click one to open it in your browser. - **Market:** the S&P 500, Nasdaq, Dow, Russell 2000 and VIX; the 10-year yield, crude oil, gold, the dollar index and Bitcoin; the 11 S&P sector ETFs by day change; and the day's top 5 gainers and losers. Click a row to chart it. - **Options:** the option chain for the current symbol, calls or puts one side at a time, for any expiry (type a YYYY-MM-DD date or pick from the list). Strikes sit above or below the current price, in-the-money rows are tagged, and each row shows last, bid/ask, change, volume, open interest, implied volatility and last trade time. Add legs from the chain to build a strategy (presets include spreads, straddles and iron condors) and see its expiration payoff, break-evens and max profit and loss. ### Watchlist Click the star next to the ticker to add or remove it. The star in the bottom bar shows starred stocks as cards with price and percent move for the current session, including pre-market or after-hours when available. Sort by change, price or volume, or switch to a heatmap whose tiles are colored by day change and sized by the magnitude of the move. Use the screener to filter by RSI, moving averages and daily change, and save filters you want to reuse. **Groups** split the watchlist into tabs such as "Tech" or "Crypto"; **All** always shows every starred stock. Click **+** and type a name to add a group. In a group tab, **Edit** shows every starred stock: click cards to add or remove them, rename the group, or **Delete** it. Unstarring a stock removes it from every group. Press `G` to cycle through All and each group (opening the Watchlist if it is closed). ### Price alerts Open **Alerts**, to the left of Technicals, to add an alert for the selected symbol. Pick a kind: **Price** (at or above or below a level, in the trading currency), **Day move %** (up or down X% from yesterday's close), **Move since armed %** (up or down X% from the price when armed), **Trailing %** or **Trailing amount** (falls by that much from the high since arming, or rises from the low). The list includes alerts for every symbol. **Pause**, **Rearm** and **Delete** manage them, **Edit** changes an alert's direction and level, and **Duplicate** copies it. Click an alert's ticker to open its chart, and filter the list by All, Armed, Triggered or Paused. Triggered alerts show the trigger price and time. By default an alert fires once and then shows **Triggered**; tick **Recurring** to keep it armed, with a cooldown in minutes (default 15) during which it stays quiet. A recurring alert needs a fresh crossing to fire again. **Regular session only** ignores extended-hours prices and checks nothing outside the regular session. Armed symbols are checked about every 15 seconds while tickr is running, including with the window closed and when viewing a different stock. The first successful price after arming or restarting establishes a baseline; the next crossing sends a native desktop notification. Move-since-armed and trailing alerts take their reference price from the first price after arming and save it, so a trailing stop breached while tickr was closed fires on the first price after restart. Extended-hours prices are used when available. Alerts and their triggered state are saved across restarts. Allow tickr notifications in your OS settings; on Windows, use an installed build for notifications. Quotes can be delayed and crossings between polls can be missed. ### Settings and keybinds The gear at the bottom left opens Settings: the global hotkey (click the field and press a new combination; **Reset** restores the default), in-window keybinds and the chart dot toggles. Esc or a click outside closes it. Keybinds are grouped by category. Click a keybind and press a new key to rebind it (an action already on that key takes the old one), or Backspace to unbind it. Keybinds are ignored while typing in a text field. | Category | Key | Action | | --- | --- | --- | | Chart | `C` | Switch line / candles | | | `L` | Cycle price scale (Lin, Log, %) | | | `I` | Cycle candle length (Auto, then the lengths the range allows) | | | `1` | Draw level (press again for Cursor) | | | `2` | Draw trendline | | | `3` | Draw text | | | `4` | Ruler | | | `5` | Pen | | | `J` | Toggle second chart | | | `Y` | Toggle bar replay | | | `H` | Open Paper trading | | | `Q` | Start random practice | | | `V` | Cycle date range | | | `R` | Refresh | | Panels | `T` | Open Technicals | | | `Z` | Analyze / re-analyze | | | `A` | Open Analysts | | | `E` | Open Earnings | | | `P` | Open Alerts | | | `M` | Open Market | | | `K` | Open Events | | | `N` | Open News | | | `O` | Open Options | | Options | `U` | Switch calls / puts | | | `D` | Next expiry date (wraps around) | | Watchlist | `W` | Toggle Watchlist | | | `X` | Next watchlist stock | | | `G` | Next watchlist group (opens the Watchlist) | | | `F` | Add stock to Watchlist | | General | `S` | Focus search | | | `B` | Previous symbol (toggles between two) | | | `,` | Toggle Settings | | Fixed | `Alt+←` | Back to the previous symbol in history | | | `Alt+→` | Forward in history | ### AI news analysis Headline tone (the dots on the chart and the News view) comes from a local keyword lexicon by default. Optionally, Settings > AI > News analysis sends new headlines to any OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint (OpenAI, Ollama, LM Studio, ...) to classify them as positive, neutral or negative. Fill in the base URL (for example `https://api.openai.com/v1`), the model and, if the endpoint needs one, the API key. The key may stay empty for local endpoints. A saved key is never sent back to the page: the field shows "Key saved", leaving it blank keeps the key, and Clear removes it. **Test connection** saves the settings and checks each configured model. Model is the master model. To use a different one for a feature, fill in News model (headline tone) or Events model (event analysis); a blank field uses Model. These are saved to `.env.local` in the settings folder (see [Files](#files)), not to `settings.json`, as `TICKR_AI_BASE_URL`, `TICKR_AI_MODEL`, `TICKR_AI_NEWS_MODEL`, `TICKR_AI_EVENTS_MODEL` and `TICKR_AI_API_KEY`; other lines in that file are left alone. Results are cached per model and headline in the cache folder, so each headline is sent once. If AI is off, not configured or a call fails, the keyword tone is used. News labels each tone **AI** or **Keyword**; hover for the model and generation time. Settings > Connections shows quote, news and AI status, last successes and readable errors, with a Retry action for each service. **Copy diagnostics** copies app and OS versions and connection details with credentials redacted. ### Market events The Events panel (header button or `K`) has two tabs. **Economic** lists seven days of releases from Yahoo's economic calendar, grouped by day, each with its local release time and, where Yahoo has them, the actual, expected and prior figures. It starts with the next 7 days; the arrows step a week back or forward (up to about a year either way) and **Today** returns. The country menu picks which countries to show (US by default, or all) and **All / Key** limits the list to headline releases (jobs, inflation, GDP, rates, PMIs, retail sales, confidence). Yahoo does not rate importance, so Key is decided by release name and is only a rough guide. Both choices are saved in settings. The list needs no AI and is refreshed every 15 minutes or with the Refresh button. **Watchlist** merges the upcoming earnings dates and ex-dividend dates of your starred symbols into one list by day, with an All / Earnings / Ex-dividend toggle. Click a row to open that symbol. Estimated earnings dates are marked and the EPS estimate is shown when Yahoo has one. Dates are cached for 6 hours and fetched three symbols at a time; ETFs, indices and crypto have none. Clicking an event asks the AI configured in Settings, as above, using the Events model or else Model, to analyze that one release: a summary and the affected stocks and sectors, each with a score, confidence and reasoning. Only the opened event is sent, along with its figures and a few current Yahoo headlines about it. Analyses are cached for 6 hours per model, and a new one is made once the actual figure is out. Details show the model and generation time; **Regenerate** requests a fresh analysis for that event. ## Screenshots The demo and screenshots use sample data. Click an image to view it at full size. | | | | :---: | :---: | | [![Five-year and one-year AAPL charts with linked crosshairs](assets/screenshots/split-charts.png)](assets/screenshots/split-charts.png)
**Linked charts** let you inspect the same date in two date ranges. | [![Historical AAPL chart with bar replay controls](assets/screenshots/bar-replay.png)](assets/screenshots/bar-replay.png)
**Bar replay** reveals candles at your pace. | | [![Replay chart with a buy fill and the simulated position panel](assets/screenshots/paper-trading.png)](assets/screenshots/paper-trading.png)
**Paper trading** shows the filled order and open position. | [![Historical practice result with return, bars held and a Skip comparison](assets/screenshots/historical-practice.png)](assets/screenshots/historical-practice.png)
**Historical practice** shows how a trade performed against skipping. | | [![AAPL candle chart with an OHLC tooltip and event markers](assets/screenshots/chart.png)](assets/screenshots/chart.png)
**Chart** shows candle details and lets you copy a PNG or CSV. | [![AAPL chart with indicator overlays, RSI and a technical analysis score](assets/screenshots/technicals.webp)](assets/screenshots/technicals.webp)
**Technicals** computes signals and targets from the chart's candles. | | [![Market overview with indices, macro quotes, sectors and movers](assets/screenshots/market.png)](assets/screenshots/market.png)
**Market** groups indices, sectors and daily movers. | [![Stock watchlist with session prices and named groups](assets/screenshots/watchlist.png)](assets/screenshots/watchlist.png)
**Watchlist** keeps prices and session moves for starred symbols together. | ## Data Quotes, charts, news and fundamentals come from Yahoo Finance's public chart, search and quoteSummary endpoints. They are not an official API and can change or rate-limit without notice, and quotes may be delayed. Logos come from [Elbstream](https://elbstream.com/logos)'s logo API (formerly Parqet); the **Logos by Elbstream** link in the footer is the attribution its free tier requires. Analysis and sentiment run on your machine. Not investment advice. ## Files | What | Windows | macOS | | --- | --- | --- | | Settings | `%APPDATA%\tickr\settings.json` | `~/Library/Application Support/tickr/` | | AI credentials | `%APPDATA%\tickr\.env.local` | `~/Library/Application Support/tickr/` | | Logo, AI tone and event analysis cache | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\tickr\` | `~/Library/Caches/tickr/` | | Logs | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dev.tickr.desktop\logs\tickr.log` | `~/Library/Logs/dev.tickr.desktop/` | Logs rotate at 1 MB and keep two old files. Attach `tickr.log` to bug reports. Uninstalling on Windows removes the launch-at-login entry. Check "Delete the application data" in the uninstaller to also remove settings, the logo cache, logs and WebView data. ## Development ### Build Requirements: Rust 1.85+, Node 20+, and the [Tauri 2 prerequisites](https://tauri.app/start/prerequisites/). ```bash npm install npm run tauri dev # dev build with hot reload npx tauri build # installer (NSIS on Windows, .app and .dmg on macOS) ``` `npx tauri build` also signs the updater bundles, which needs the private key (see [Updater key](#updater-key)). Without it, skip the updater artifacts: ```bash npx tauri build -c '{"bundle":{"createUpdaterArtifacts":false}}' ``` The Windows installer installs per user (no UAC prompt), in English. On macOS, `src-tauri/Info.plist` sets `LSUIElement` so tickr never shows a Dock icon; the minimum version is macOS 10.15. ### Releasing Releases are built by GitHub Actions. Bump the version in `package.json`, `src-tauri/Cargo.toml` and `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry, then push a tag: ```bash git tag v0.11.2 git push origin v0.11.2 ``` `.github/workflows/release.yml` builds the Windows NSIS installer and a universal macOS `.app`/`.dmg` with `tauri-apps/tauri-action`, and attaches them to a **draft** release for that tag, along with the signed updater bundles and `latest.json`. Failed asset uploads are retried twice. A last job checks that `latest.json` lists Windows and both macOS architectures; if it fails, re-run the failed jobs from the Actions tab, which re-uploads into the same draft. Review the notes and publish the release from the Releases page. Installed copies only see it once it is published and marked latest (not a pre-release), because the updater reads `releases/latest/download/latest.json`. #### Updater key Updates are signed with a minisign key pair, separate from code signing and free. The public key is `plugins.updater.pubkey` in `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`. The private key stays off the repo, in `~/.tauri/tickr.key`, and CI reads it from the `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` repository secret. Set it to the file's contents, unchanged (one base64 line): ```bash gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY < ~/.tauri/tickr.key ``` The key has no password, so leave `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD` unset. If the secret is missing or mangled, tauri fails at the end of the build with "Missing comment in secret key"; the release workflow checks the secret first and fails right away instead. Back the key up somewhere safe. If it is lost, installed copies reject every future update and users have to reinstall by hand. A local `npx tauri build` needs the same two variables, or it fails at the updater signing step. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `npm run check`, `npm test`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` (Windows and macOS) on every push to `main` and every pull request. #### Code signing Releases are not code-signed yet (see [First launch](#first-launch)). macOS builds are ad-hoc signed (`bundle.macOS.signingIdentity: "-"`), so Gatekeeper reports an unidentified developer rather than a damaged app. Signing needs certificates, so it is set up through environment variables at build time rather than in the repo. **macOS** needs a Developer ID Application certificate in the keychain and an Apple ID app-specific password (or an App Store Connect API key) for notarization. Remove `"signingIdentity": "-"` from `tauri.conf.json` first; `tauri build` signs, notarizes and staples when these are set: ```bash export APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY="Developer ID Application: Your Name (TEAMID)" export APPLE_ID="you@example.com" export APPLE_PASSWORD="REDACTED" export APPLE_TEAM_ID="TEAMID" npx tauri build --target universal-apple-darwin ``` **Windows** can use an Authenticode certificate (set `bundle.windows.certificateThumbprint`, `digestAlgorithm: "sha256"` and a `timestampUrl` in `tauri.conf.json`) or Azure Trusted Signing (set `bundle.windows.signCommand` to a `trusted-signing-cli` call). See [Windows code signing](https://v2.tauri.app/distribute/sign/windows/) and [macOS code signing](https://v2.tauri.app/distribute/sign/macos/). In CI, add the Apple values as repository secrets (plus `APPLE_CERTIFICATE`, the base64 `.p12`, and `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`) and uncomment them in `release.yml`. `npm run icon` regenerates the app icons from `scripts/make-icon.mjs`. ### Tests ```bash cd src-tauri && cargo test # technical analysis (indicators, patterns, Fibonacci, scoring), quote, analyst, earnings, rating change, stats, financials, market and news parsing, headline sentiment, sessions, tray tooltip and title, icon compositing, settings, watchlist symbols and groups, economic calendar and watchlist dates, update menu labels cd src-tauri && cargo test -- --ignored live # anal

# codex-delegate

Offload bounded work to Codex. Claude stays orchestrator and reviewer.

Delegate when ALL hold:
- Spec fits in one self-contained prompt (no need for this chat's history).

- Verifiable by a command (tests, build, lint) or by reading the diff.
- Not security-sensitive, not architecture, not a subtle/concurrency bug.

Good fits: test suites, boilerplate, docs/README, mechanical refactors, small features with clear spec, second-opinion review, codebase Q&A.
Keep in Claude: design decisions, ambiguous requirements, cross-repo changes, debugging that needs iteration.

## Gate (automatic)

`codex-run.ps1` runs `codex-gate.ps1` first. It blocks (exit 3, `GATE_BLOCKED: <why>`) unless the Codex login is on the **plus** plan and neither the 5h nor weekly window is >= 95% used (read from the newest `~/.codex/sessions` rate_limits entry; a window past its reset counts as 0%). On block: do the task yourself or with a normal subagent. Do not retry in a loop. Check without running: `& "<skill dir>\codex-gate.ps1"`.

## Model choice (Claude decides, always medium effort)

- `gpt-6.1-sol` (default): routine work: tests, boilerplate, docs, mechanical refactors, small clear features, reviews.
- `gpt-6-astra`: harder medium work: several interacting files, some ambiguity, tricky logic. Costs more usage; if the task needs more than this, keep it in Claude.

Pass with `-Model gpt-6-astra`.

## How

Run the wrapper (PowerShell). The scripts sit next to this SKILL.md; use this skill's base directory as `<skill dir>`:

```powershell
& "<skill dir>\codex-run.ps1" -Prompt "<task>" -Cwd "<project dir>" [-Write] [-Model gpt-6.1-sol|gpt-6-astra] [-TimeoutSec 600]
```

- Default is read-only sandbox (review, research, analysis).
- `-Write` = `workspace-write` sandbox: Codex may edit files inside `-Cwd` only.
- Long jobs: run with `run_in_background` and wait for the notification.
- Output = Codex's final message. On failure prints `CODEX_FAILED` / `CODEX_TIMEOUT` plus stderr tail.

## Prompt template

Codex has no access to this conversation. Include:
1. Goal (one sentence).
2. Exact files/dirs in scope, and what NOT to touch.
3. Conventions to follow (point at an example file).
4. Done criteria + verify command (e.g. `npm test`).
5. "Do not commit. Report changed files and anything unverified."

1. `git diff` / `git status` in the project. Read the diff.

- One Codex job per file set at a time; no parallel writers on same files.

2	
3	A wearable backpack for Alex Chen (47, ALS) that counteracts his gait and balance problems so he can keep teaching: it senses trunk tilt and sway, taps his torso and speaks cues through a phone app when fatigue or foot-drop sway is detected, and streams data to a clinician dashboard with AI-generated reports. 5	## Event facts
6	
7	- Event: BioHacks 2026 by BioEng4Youth, McMaster University, Hamilton. Official MLH Member Event.
8	- Format: every team solves one patient-centred neurological case, revealed at the opening ceremony. Pitches should be clear and evidence-backed. Judges come from sponsors and partners.
9	- Sat Nov 7: opening 10:00 AM, team formation 11:00 AM, team registration and track lock-in closes 12:00 PM.

11	- Work must be made during the event. Software, hardware, 3D prints and design concepts are all accepted.
12	- Devpost submission needs: problem description, how it works, what was built, links to code/CAD/slides, a short video demo, every teammate added, and a track selection matching the team form.
13	- Devpost: https://devpost.com/submit-to/30296-biohacks-2026/manage/submissions
14	
15	## Tracks and prizes
16	
17	Each team competes in exactly one track. Sponsor prizes are opted into at submission. Wearables rubric (out of 100): clinical grounding 20, design and function 30 (prototype or demo counts), usability in daily life 20, feasibility 15, communication 15. $1,000 goes to the top team overall.
18

22	- Best Use of Tiger Data: judged on innovative, impactful and performance-driven use.

27	## Locked decisions
28	
29	- Pitch goal: staying in a classroom in June 2027. Target moments: walking around the room and standing at the board, with late-day fatigue in mind.
30	- Mechanism is hybrid. (1) Working wearable: cues timed to the gait cycle plus spoken cues when fatigue or foot-drop sway is detected. (2) Tabletop gyroscope rig: a spinning flywheel on a servo gimbal that physically resists a tipping dummy torso, showing the active-correction version, based on TU Delft's GyBAR (see `PATIENT_CASE.md`).
31	- Form factor stays a backpack: as light as possible, no chest pressure, closures usable without fine finger control.
32	- Haptics are servo tappers, not vibration motors. The MLH hardware lab has no vibration motors or haptic drivers. Servo split: 2 Grove Servos as left/right tappers, 1 as the rig's gimbal, 1 spare. The Grove Buzzer is a piezo and cannot vibrate against the body.

34	- No moving weights. Shifting a small mass barely moves the center of mass, adds mechanical risk, and could destabilize the wearer.

40	- Tiger Data (TimescaleDB): all four ideas, with focus on (1) high-frequency IMU ingestion into a hypertable with continuous aggregates per minute/hour/day and (3) anomaly-window queries that flag unusual sway and feed Gemini. 41	- Vultr: level 1 is the VM hosting the real-time pipeline, with live tilt-to-voice latency shown on the dashboard. Stretch: train a small sway classifier on a Vultr GPU instance from labeled data (stable, swaying, near-fall) and serve it from the VM.

1	# Patient Case: Alex Chen (ALS)
2	
3	Source: https://www.bioeng4youth.ca/BioHacks-2026-Hacker-Package.pdf (fictional case provided by BioHacks 2026). This is a working summary for design decisions; check the PDF for exact wording before quoting it in the pitch.
4	
5	## Who he is
6	
7	- 47, male, right-handed. Senior biology teacher at a Hamilton high school for 19 years. Former cross-country coach and half-marathon runner; stopped running in spring 2025.
8	- Lives in Westdale with partner Jordan (medical radiation technologist, 7 AM to 4 PM shifts) and children Maya (16) and Leo (14).
9	- Two-storey house. Bedroom and the only full bathroom are upstairs, 14 stairs.
10	
11	## Diagnosis and course
12	
13	- Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), limb onset, with early bulbar and respiratory involvement. Diagnosed 14 July 2026 after about 27 months of symptoms.
14	- June 2024: whiteboard handwriting faded; right thumb and index finger fatigued quickly. Carpal tunnel release (Jan 2025) did not help despite normal wrist studies.
15	- Spring 2025: right foot drop, progressing despite physiotherapy. Then falls, a cane, and spreading weakness.
16	- Tests: EMG shows widespread active denervation in four regions with normal sensory conduction. CK mildly raised (470 U/L). Neurofilament light chain 88 pg/mL (reference below 15). Genetic panel negative (C9orf72, SOD1, TARDBP, FUS and 28 others). MRI shows corticospinal tract changes and a motor band sign.
17	- Prognosis as communicated: median survival two to four years from onset, wide range. Feeding tube, night ventilation and communication decisions are better made early.
18	
19	## Current status (September 2026)
20	
21	- ALSFRS-R 32/48, declining about 0.6 points per month.
22	- Grip: right 3/5 with pinch lasting only seconds; left 4/5 and weakening. Uses a spoon in the left hand. Handwriting illegible after about ten minutes. Needs help with buttons, zips and shoelaces in the morning.
23	- Speech intelligible but effortful by late afternoon. Reading rate drops from 165 wpm at 9 AM to 118 wpm at 4 PM; sentence intelligibility from 98% to 91%.
24	- Swallowing: coughs on thin liquids; solids and thickened liquids fine. Meals take 35 to 40 minutes. Weight down from 86 kg to 77.5 kg. Calorie supplement started.
25	- Breathing: FVC 76% sitting, 61% supine. Sleeps on two pillows.
26	- Cognition: reduced verbal fluency and executive function; memory, language and visuospatial scores normal.
27	- Mobility: two falls in three months, both after 6 PM, on the stairs or at dusk. 10 m walk in 14.2 s with a cane. Wears a right ankle-foot orthosis at school but not at home.
28	- Medications: riluzole 50 mg twice daily since July 2026 (tolerated). Edaravone declined for now.
29	
30	## Daily life
31	
32	- Still teaches four classes a day. Has not taken up the stool or microphone the school offered.
33	- Drives an automatic with his left foot; has not told his insurer.
34	- Alone at home on non-teaching days and from the end of school until 4:30 PM.
35	- Has declined a stairlift "for now". Stopped eating in the staff room and stopped the end-of-day recap.
36	
37	## Goals
38	
39	- Stay in a classroom in June 2027.
40	- Keep cooking Sunday family meals, even if it takes all afternoon.
41	- Be "reachable and useful" while alone in the afternoons.
42	- Attend his daughter's graduation in two years without a wheelchair.
43	- Be remembered by his children as their dad, not as a patient.
44	
45	## Reluctances
46	
47	- Voice banking ("it feels like giving up").
48	- Stairlift.
49	- Asking for classroom accommodations.
50	
51	## Care team
52	
53	Dr. Priya Raman (family physician), Dr. Marcus Oyelaran (plastic and hand surgery), Daniela Ferreira (physiotherapist), Dr. Hannah Weiss-Okafor (neurologist), Dr. Thanh Nguyen (neuroradiology), a regional ALS clinic every three months, plus speech-language pathology, dietitian, occupational therapy, respiratory, social work and ALS Canada.
54	
55	## Wearables track prompt
56	
57	Design a device or tool that helps Alex keep one thing that matters to him as his abilities change. The organizers highlight his afternoon weakness, needing to be heard in class, being alone until 4:30 PM, his falls on the stairs, and the risk that assistive devices go unused when nobody asks the user what they want. The MLH hardware lab is open all weekend.
58	
59	## Wearables rubric (out of 100)
60	
61	- Clinical grounding: 20
62	- Design and function: 30, including whether a prototype or demonstration supports it
63	- Usability in daily life: 20, including comfort, adapting as the condition progresses, and day-to-day use
64	- Feasibility: 15
65	- Communication: 15
66	
67	Each criterion has four levels. Judges score each project and name their top three; combined rankings pick two winners per track. There is also $1,000 for the top team overall.
68	
69	## Design implications for our project
70	
71	- Goal we center on: staying in a classroom in June 2027. Target moments are walking around the room (between desks and the board) and standing at the board, both of which get harder as weakness and fatigue build through the afternoon.
72	- Intent: counteract the gait and balance problem rather than cure it, so Alex can keep walking and standing while teaching with a much lower fall risk.
73	- His falls come from motor weakness (right foot drop, fatigue) with normal sensory conduction, not a sensory or vestibular deficit. Tactile cues alone are weakly grounded for ALS, which is why the concept pairs cues with active correction.
74	- Active correction precedent: TU Delft's GyBAR, a backpack-like control moment gyroscope that applies corrective moments to the trunk (Lemus et al., Scientific Reports 2020, DOI 10.1038/s41598-020-66760-w). Tested on healthy and chronic stroke participants, not ALS, so present it as a promising direction, not proven for Alex.
75	- Risk is time-dependent: weakness and speech worsen through the afternoon, and both falls were after 6 PM, on stairs or at dusk. Time-of-day trends belong in the data and the reports.
76	- Form factor stays a backpack. Keep it as light as possible and put no pressure on the chest, given his weight loss (86 to 77.5 kg) and reduced FVC (76% sitting, 61% supine). Closures and controls must not need fine finger control (no small buttons, zips or clasps).
77	- He resists visible assistive devices and classroom accommodations. The device should look like a normal backpack and stay discreet in front of students, and the pitch should show we designed around what he wants.
78	- The ALS clinic sees him every three months. Continuous between-visit data (sway, gait changes, time-of-day patterns) summarized for the physio and neurologist is the clinical value of the Gemini reports.
79	- ElevenLabs is for spoken cues only. Voice banking is a stated reluctance, so never clone his voice or frame the audio as voice banking.
80	- Relevant dataset: Gait in Neurodegenerative Disease (PhysioNet), foot-force and stride data including ALS, open download. Could inform thresholds or the stretch sway classifier.

- Pitch goal: staying in a classroom in June 2027 and not falling on the stairs at home. Target moments: walking between desks and the board late in the school day, and the 14 stairs at home after 6 PM, when both of his falls happened.

- Adaptation: lift assist rises automatically with fatigue, when toe clearance drops. Clearance target is 2 cm; 1.2 cm is the risk threshold used by the forecast.
- Sensing: ankle angle (dorsiflexion positive), toe clearance per swing, gait events (toe-off, cadence, stride time), terrain (level, stairs up, stairs down), assist level, and on/off wear status. The Pi samples at about 100 Hz; the dashboard live stream is throttled to 20 Hz.
- Raspberry Pi 4B is the brain. It has WiFi built in, reads the Grove 3-axis accelerometer over I2C, drives the assist servo (directly or via the Grove Motor/Servo Driver Board), and runs from a USB-C power bank. - PhysioNet Gait in Neurodegenerative Disease database: ALS and control stride time and stride variability calibrate how far Alex's gait sits between healthy and ALS reference values.
- Gemini reports: a plain weekly summary for family (automatic every Monday) and an on-demand physician report over a chosen range with stability findings, progression versus baseline, suggested physiotherapy focus and questions for the next visit. # 3-Minute Pitch: Adaptive Ankle-Foot Brace

Target length: about 420 spoken words, 3:00 at a calm pace. Timestamps are cumulative. Lines in **bold** are actions at the table.

## 0:00 to 0:30 | The problem

Alex Chen is 47. He has taught biology in Hamilton for 19 years, and he has ALS. His goal is simple: still be in a classroom in June 2027.

The biggest thing in the way is his right foot. Foot drop means his toe catches the floor. He has fallen twice in three months, both times after 6 PM, on the stairs or at dusk. That timing is the clue: his ankle is weakest when he is most tired.

## 0:30 to 1:10 | The idea

He already wears a brace at school, a passive ankle-foot orthosis. It gives the same help at 9 AM as at 9 PM, and he leaves it off at home, where both falls happened.

So we built an adaptive brace. It measures ankle angle and toe clearance on every step, knows when he is on stairs, and raises its lift assist as fatigue lowers his clearance. It stays under his trousers, with no buttons or buckles to fight with weak fingers. No new visible device, which matters to a man who has turned down a stool, a microphone and a stairlift.

## 1:10 to 2:10 | Demo

**Open the dashboard in Physician mode.**

The brace streams from a Raspberry Pi into Tiger Data. Here is his live ankle trace and the assist level. Every evening, clearance drops and assist climbs to keep his toe above the 2 centimetre target.

**Press `n` in the simulator to force a stair near-trip.**

That near-trip is logged, and in Family mode Jordan sees a calm banner, not a siren. Alex is alone until 4:30 most days, and he wants to stay reachable without being watched.

**Switch to the heatmap, then the forecast.**

This heatmap is 14 days by hour: the red band is every evening. The forecast fits 90 days of data and projects when his evening clearance will cross the 1.2 centimetre risk line. We calibrate his stride against ALS and control patients from the PhysioNet gait database, and match today against his most similar past days.

**Generate a Gemini physician report.**

Gemini turns three months of data into findings, progression since baseline, suggested physiotherapy focus and questions for his next clinic visit. It is labelled as suggestions for his physiotherapist, not a diagnosis.

## 2:10 to 2:40 | Why it works

His clinic sees him every three months. This fills the gap between visits with real data from his real day. Tiger Data hypertables, continuous aggregates and compression keep 90 days of step-level data fast to query. And as ALS progresses, the brace does not get replaced; it adjusts.

## 2:40 to 3:00 | Close

AFOs are standard care for foot drop. We made one that notices when he is tired and helps more, and lets the people who care about him see it.

Alex wants his students to remember a teacher, not a patient. This brace keeps him on his feet long enough for that.

## Likely judge questions

- **Is adaptive assist proven for ALS?** No. AFOs are standard for foot drop; adaptive assist is a prototype. We present it as a promising direction.
- **How is toe clearance measured?** From the ankle angle and gait events on the Pi. The demo uses a simulator that posts the same data the Pi does.
- **Why not just cues or alarms?** His falls come from motor weakness, not missing sensation. A cue does not lift the foot; the brace does.
- **What happens as he gets weaker?** Assist rises over months, the forecast shows when, and the physician report flags it before the next visit.

Physicians see live ankle movement, gait trends, clinic scores, forecasts and Gemini reports. A simulator and seeded history let the dashboard run without brace hardware. ## Features ### Family view - **Today:** a plain-language status sentence, brace wear status and last update, plus a 7 AM to 10 PM timeline of stair bouts, possible trips and falls. - **Week:** a stability score out of 100, a seven-day sparkline, comparison with the previous week and the latest family report. - **Check-in alerts:** new near-trip and fall events open an in-page sheet with an "I've checked in" button and a soft Web Audio chime. Browser audio needs a user interaction first. ### Physician view - **Live monitoring:** a rolling ten-second ankle-angle trace, last-step toe clearance against a 2 cm target, assist percentage, terrain and brace wear status. - **Period comparisons:** select 7, 30 or 90 days for stability, average clearance, peak dorsiflexion, assist and near-trips per 100 stair steps, with changes against the previous period. - **Progression:** 90-day charts for stability, clearance, dorsiflexion and assist, with clinic visit markers. The clearance chart adds daily percentile bands and a downsampled hourly trace. - **Clinic visits:** enter a date, ALSFRS-R score, 10 m walk time and optional note; saved visits appear in a table. - **Time-of-day patterns:** a 14-day clearance heatmap with near-trip markers and hover details. Filter the event list by near-trip, fall, assist change or stairs. - **Similar days:** compare the latest qualifying gait day with three older days, using standardized clearance, dorsiflexion, stride variability and assist. A separate exploratory indicator compares stride timing with PhysioNet control and ALS cohort averages. - **Forecast:** project clearance, evening clearance, ankle lift, assist and stride variability for 90 days, with uncertainty bands, threshold crossing estimates and backtest results when enough history exists. These are statistical extrapolations, not clinical predictions. - **Data engine:** inspect recent ingest throughput, measured raw versus daily-rollup query times and database compression statistics. ### Reports and display - **Gemini reports:** generate a physician report for the selected range and reopen past reports in a side sheet. Recommendations are framed as suggestions for the treating physiotherapist to review, and reports display "AI-generated summary, not medical advice." - **View preferences:** the Family / Physician selection is saved in browser local storage. It accepts timestamped ankle-angle samples, per-step clearance, dorsiflexion, stride time, assist level and terrain, plus care events. The backend receives these measurements; the repository does not include Raspberry Pi firmware or the physical brace controller. Next, on the Pi:
```bash
pip install -r pi/requirements.txt
```
```bash
python pi/stream.py --url http://<server-ip>:3000/api/ingest --assist 50
```
Stand still for the first 2 seconds while it calibrates.

**What the Pi script does** ([pi/stream.py](pi/stream.py))
- Reads the MMA7660FC (I2C address 0x4C) at 100 Hz. Shank tilt from the filtered gravity vector, minus the standing calibration, is sent as `ankleDeg`.
- Detects steps on the Pi, each with stride time, peak swing angle, terrain `level`, and an estimated toe clearance.
- Assist is a fixed value set with `--assist`. It doesn't control a servo.
- Sends a batch to `/api/ingest` about every 250 ms from a background thread. If the network drops, it keeps up to about 30 seconds of data and retries, and the sampling loop keeps running.
- `--fake` makes up a swing signal so you can test on a laptop. [pi/README.md](pi/README.md) has the wiring, how to enable I2C, and an `i2cdetect` check where 4c should appear.

**What I tested**
- `python pi/test_stream.py` passes.
- I ran `--fake` against a local listener that mimics the server. It made about 4 requests a second, each with about 26 samples. Steps came out about once a second with a stride time of about 1000 ms, and the fields match what `/api/ingest` accepts.
- I didn't point it at the real server, so no rows were written to the database. It hasn't run on real Pi hardware.

**Things to know**
- **Not a true ankle angle:** the sensor sits on the shank, so it measures shank tilt.
- **Clearance is a guess:** there's no distance sensor, so clearance is worked out from peak swing. I retuned the constants so a swing of about 25° gives about 20 mm (Codex's first values gave about 46 mm). Check this against real walking.
- **Stairs not detected:** every step is reported as `level`.
- **Cleanup won't remove Pi rows:** `seed:clear` keeps them; delete them with `seed:clear -- --all`.
